messages:
ava_se: Quick alert 10: ZenithHealth POC stream is dropping during a live demo. They get HTML error fragments in the SSE stream and the browser JSON parser fails. Need triage ASAP before tomorrow's exec demo.

tom_support: Can you share the request id and the exact client error? Also confirm whether this is hosted or dedicated and which model.

ava_se: request_id=zh_4b9d1a, hosted, model=redwood-7b. Client error in console: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0" when handling SSE message. Uses EventSource in React (latest Chrome).

li_dev: That token '<' usually means an HTML error page is being injected mid-stream (502/504 from a proxy or edge). Can you paste the raw stream capture?

emma_reliability: I pulled edge logs for zh_4b9d1a:

```
2026-03-18T09:03:22Z INFO stream.start req=zh_4b9d1a tenant=zenith
2026-03-18T09:03:24Z INFO chunk.send req=zh_4b9d1a bytes=1024
2026-03-18T09:03:25Z WARN upstream.error req=zh_4b9d1a code=502 backend=proxy-east
2026-03-18T09:03:25Z INFO stream.abort req=zh_4b9d1a reason=upstream_error
```

The runtime closed because the edge returned 502. We see an HTML payload in our logs at the tail of the stream.

zenith_ops (guest): We captured tcpdump. After ~6s our infra returns a 502 with an HTML payload that begins with "<html>". We have a custom WAF/proxy that might be cutting connections on certain response sizes.

li_dev: Two parallel failure modes: 1) upstream proxy returns an error page mid-stream; 2) connection gets reset and client ends up parsing partial JSON. Repro curl (from inside Zenith network):

```
curl -sv -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-7b"
```

Look for initial comment keepalives and then final "event: done". If you see HTML in between, it's the proxy/WAF.

tom_support: Zenith ran curl and attached stream dump: first two events are ok, then a chunk starts with `<html>` and connection closes. They also reported occasional 429 before the HTML which suggests their proxy may be rate-limiting and returning an HTML error page instead of a JSON 429 event.

emma_reliability: For mitigation we can offer: 
- Short term: enable explicit SSE boundary events and send periodic comment keepalives (server-side) so proxies see traffic (we have a candidate patch).
- Client-side: switch EventSource handler to do incremental assembly of 'data' lines and ignore non-JSON events, or use our SDK which tolerates unexpected chunks.
- Infra change: ask Zenith to configure WAF to return JSON 429s or allow long-lived connections and disable body injection mid-stream.

li_dev: Candidate we pushed to staging: sse-heartbeat-v1 (adds `:hb\n\n` keepalive every 10s and final `event: finished\ndata: [DONE]\n\n`). Deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T09:45Z.
deploy-bot: [eng-releases] sse-heartbeat-v1 deployed to staging by li_dev at 2026-03-18T09:45Z. Runbook: set `stream.keepalive_secs=10` and `stream.final_event=true`.

ava_se: Can we run that on a shared POC route for Zenith? They'll test and report back. Zenith is asking about timelines and cost for Redwood to push the change to their POC endpoint vs them changing WAF.

tom_support: Recommend messaging: 1) quickest: Zenith tweak WAF to stop injecting HTML for streaming paths (typically a config change, <1 day). 2) Redwood hotfix to emit keepalives and explicit end event (we can do as a POC deploy within 24 hours, no charge for POC). 3) Long-term: move to dedicated route or use our SDK and monitoring for production (cost varies by committed capacity).

zenith_ops (guest): We'll try WAF tweak first and retest. If that fails, please stage the heartbeat patch on our POC route.

li_dev: Action items: - (li_dev) instrument telemetry to detect HTML-in-stream and tag events HTML_INJECTION - (emma_reliability) add alert if stream abort rate > 0.5% tenant-wide - (tom_support) open support ticket linking logs and staging candidate - (ava_se) update presales doc to list proxy/WAF as common POC blocker and mitigation steps.

ava_se: Thanks everyone. Zenith will try the WAF change and post the curl dump here. If they still see injection we'll coordinate a staging push. :pray:
